Additionally, about 9 MW of power can be produced by a back-pressure turbine due to the conversion of high-pressure steam to low-pressure steam required for the project. However, this can not match the total steam and power requirement. So, a combined heat and power unit and a steam boiler are still needed to cater to the steam and power requirements for the project. Two capacity options have been evaluated. 1) a bigger single unit of 260 tonnes/hr capacity, and 2) two smaller units of 130 tonnes/hr capacity. However, both options have been discarded. Option 1, i.e., 260 tonnes/hr, cannot match the sequence of coking, and space is not available for two 130 tonnes/hr of coke dry quenching facilities. Therefore, the coke dry quenching has not been considered for the project. e) Combined Heat and Power Unit along with LP Boiler: Given the requirement of both electricity and steam, a combined heat and power unit (CHP) is the most suitable option for sourcing both steam and electricity for the project. Dastur has selected 58 MW GT for the project, which will supply most of the electricity required for the project, and high-pressure steam, which needs to be converted to low-pressure steam necessary for the project. A 15 MW Back-Pressure Turbine (BPT) has been considered to convert high-pressure steam to low-pressure steam. While reducing the steam duty, BPT will generate power that can be utilized for the project facilities. Since the steam requirement is significantly higher compared to the power requirement, separate LP boilers have been considered to fulfill the LP steam requirement. 3.0 Configuration for Steam and Electricity Generation Unit for the Project Given the requirement for both steam and electricity, the following units have been considered for the project: 1. CHP Unit: To generate 58 MW of electricity and about 400 MMBtu/hr steam 2. BPT Unit: To reduce 615 PSIA steam to 60 PSIA steam and generate 15 MW of electricity 3. Steam boilers: To generate about 900 MMBtu/hr low-pressure steam The steam and electricity sourcing flow diagram is given in Figure 2.
